00

Before the session

Carried over from Day 1

Nothing new to produce here. If Day 1 (Business Authority Foundation) was completed, everyone already has what this session needs.

The four foundation documents
01ICP Document
02Messaging House
03Brand Positioning
04Business Inbox

If they also produced the Rule of 1, that goes in too. It carries the single villain, the single outcome, and the hooks, which is the fastest route to a headline that doesn't read like filler.

Plus, whatever brand material already exists
  • Logo file, any format
  • Existing photos: headshots, work shots, product or premises images
  • Brand colors, hex codes if they have them, or described in plain language
  • Fonts they already use, if any
If any of this is missing Don't send anyone back to redo Day 1 live. Missing brand colors, fonts, or a logo isn't a blocker, Step 04's prompt has Claude propose them. Missing the foundation documents entirely is the one true blocker; have that person pull them up before Step 01.
01

Create the project folder

5 min
  1. On the desktop, create one new folder named for both their business and their personal brand, e.g. summit-ridge-malik-website. This keeps the folder identifiable if they're managing more than one project later.
  2. Drop every foundation document from Step 00 straight into this folder, no sub-folders needed.
  3. Add the logo, every photo they want on the site, and a plain text note with their brand colors and fonts if those aren't already written down somewhere. A media sub-folder is fine if they'd rather keep it tidy, Claude will find both.
Confirm before moving on Every participant's folder should contain the foundation docs plus every image and colour reference they have, before anyone opens Claude Code. Anything added after the build starts tends to get ignored, so this is the one step worth a visible round of confirmation in chat.
02

Open the folder in Claude Code

3 min
  1. Open Claude Desktop, click the Code tab (next to Chat and Cowork), then New Session.
  2. Click Open Folder, select the folder built in Step 01, and click Trust Workspace when prompted.

Everyone's folder tab at the top should now show their business and personal brand folder name. Don't advance until every screen shows this.

03

Install the design skill

8 minOne-time onlyVerified against Anthropic docs

One skill, UI/UX Pro Max: a library of colour palettes, font pairings, and layout patterns for Claude to pull from. This is the difference between a site that looks like everyone else's AI output and one that doesn't, say that out loud, it's why the room shouldn't skip it. Installed once, it's available automatically in every future project, with no reinstalling per session.

The click path below is the confirmed one from Anthropic's own plugin documentation, so it should match what's on screen exactly. Walk it slowly, this is the step where a quiet failure costs the most later.

Part A: Add the marketplace
Left sidebar→ Customize→ Plugins tab→ "+" button→ Add marketplace
  1. Click Customize in the left sidebar. This is the single home for plugins, skills, and connectors, everything for this step lives here.
  2. Open the Plugins tab.
  3. In the Personal plugins section, click the "+" button.
  4. Select Add marketplace.
  5. Choose Add from a repository, the option that accepts a GitHub URL directly rather than picking from Anthropic's pre-built list.
Part B: Sync UI/UX Pro Max

Paste this repo URL into the field:

https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill
  1. Paste the URL, click the Use "https://github.com/..." suggestion under the field, then click Sync. This registers the marketplace but does not install anything yet.
  2. Back in the Plugins panel, click Browse at the top right. The Directory opens.
  3. Open the Code tab, select the ui-ux-pro-max-skill chip, then click the "+" on the Ui ux pro max card to install it.
Part C: Confirm it's live

Type / in the chat box, or click the "+" next to the message field. UI/UX Pro Max should appear in the list that pops up. That's the real confirmation, not the install button, an install can silently fail to register.

Confirm before Step 04 Have everyone type / and read out loud what shows up. A missed install is invisible until the finished site looks generic, and by then it's a rebuild rather than a quick fix. Don't move the room forward until every screen shows the skill.
04

The two prompts

30–40 minBuild, then elevate

Two prompts, in order, and nothing else. The first builds the entire site from the foundation documents. The second is the one that makes it look expensive: it fixes the copy, kills the AI tells, locks the palette to their real brand colours, and adds motion. Read both aloud line by line; participants adapt the bracketed fields as they type. Long prompts are the point, a short prompt is exactly how generic sites happen.

Setup, before typing anything
  1. Type / and select UI/UX Pro Max, so the palette and pattern library is active.
  2. Set the mode to Auto at the bottom of the chat, so the build runs through without stopping for permission on every file.
  3. Type or voice-to-text Prompt 1, filling in the highlighted fields.
Prompt 1: Build the draft
Please build me a complete business website for [BUSINESS NAME], based here in [CITY, COUNTRY]. Use the UI/UX Pro Max skill for this build. Layout, typography, and colour decisions should come from that skill, not from generic defaults. Everything you need is in this project folder. Read all of it before writing a single line of copy: - ICP document - Messaging House - Brand Positioning - Business Inbox - Rule of 1, if it is in the folder - My logo, my photos, and my brand colours and fonts Pull my actual positioning, my real offer, and my ICP's own language directly from those documents. Do not invent generic copy and do not paraphrase them into something vaguer. Every headline, subhead, and call to action should trace back to a specific line in one of those documents. The site should read like it was written by someone who has actually read my brand foundation, not like a template with my name dropped in. Use my logo and my own photos throughout. Build the palette from my brand colours. If I have not given you colours or fonts, propose a palette and a font pairing that fit my positioning, and tell me why you chose them. Sections I want included: [list anything specific, before and after work, a process breakdown, testimonials, service list, pricing] Build this as a single HTML file so it is simple to deploy. Before you write anything, tell me which specific lines from my documents you plan to use for the headline and the About section, so I can confirm before you build the rest.

If Claude comes back with questions before it builds, have participants answer straight from the Messaging House and Business Inbox rather than typing anything new from memory. Let it run, a first full draft typically takes 5 to 10 minutes.

Prompt 2: Elevate it

Run this immediately after the first draft, before anyone starts hand-editing. First-pass output from any model carries the same tells: em dashes everywhere, safe adjectives, flat sections, no motion. This single prompt handles all of it in one pass.

Now take this site from a draft to something that looks like a premium, high-end, high-tech website. Work through all of the following in one pass. Copy: - Remove every em dash and en dash from the site. Rewrite those sentences properly with commas, full stops, or colons instead. - Flag anything that reads as generic AI-written text: vague claims, safe adjectives, sentences that could apply to any business in my industry, phrasing that does not sound like a real person talking about their own business. - Rewrite each of those using the actual language from my Messaging House and Brand Positioning. If a claim is not supported by something in my documents, cut it or replace it with one that is. - Keep sentences short and specific, in my ICP's own words rather than marketing speak. Design, using the UI/UX Pro Max skill: - Align every colour on the site to my actual brand colours. No off-brand accents, no default blues, no stock gradients that were not my choice. - Check the font pairing against the library and apply a stronger, more specific pairing for a [BUSINESS INDUSTRY] business if there is one. - Make it far more visually appealing: better spacing, stronger hierarchy, a hero section that actually holds attention, and section transitions that do not all look identical. - Keep my logo and my photos as the anchor. Do not replace them, make everything around them look intentional. Motion: - Add smooth, tasteful animation where it earns its place: scroll reveals, hover states, a considered hero entrance, subtle parallax if it suits the layout. - Nothing that bounces, flashes, or delays what I am trying to read. Respect reduced motion preferences. Then tell me what you changed and what you cut, before I look at it.
Say this to the room Two prompts is the whole build. Anyone tempted to fire off a third or fourth ad-hoc request should hold it until they've actually looked at the file in Step 05, most of what they'd ask for is already handled by Prompt 2.
05

Open the site file

3 min
  1. Open the project folder from Step 01 on the desktop.
  2. Find the HTML file Claude built, usually index.html.
  3. Double-click it. The site opens in the default browser, full size, exactly as a visitor would see it.

Have everyone scroll their own site top to bottom once, out loud on the call, one thing they like and one thing they'd change. This surfaces the common fixes early and normalises a rough first pass, non-technical participants often read one as a personal miss rather than the normal starting point.

Before deploying Confirm every real business detail is correct: phone number, email, service list, hours, contact method. Placeholder text survives to a live URL surprisingly often, because nobody checks it while the design still has their attention.
06

Deploy, claim, and make it public

12–18 minNo domain purchase required

No hosting plan to buy, no terminal, no checkout flow. This gets a real, shareable HTTPS link in minutes on a free subdomain. A custom domain can be connected later if someone wants one.

Netlify DropRun this live
app.netlify.com/drop→ Drag the HTML file in→ Claim this site→ Sign up with Google→ Make public→ Open the live URL
  1. Go to app.netlify.com/drop in a browser.
  2. Drag index.html from the project folder straight into the drop zone. The file link underneath does the same thing for anyone whose drag does not land.
  1. The site goes live and returns a URL like https://gorgeous-praline-f5ac32.netlify.app.
  2. Claim it. Until it is claimed the deploy is temporary: it expires in one hour and sits behind a placeholder password. Click Claim this site, in either the banner or the panel below it.
  1. Choose Sign up with Google and complete the sign-in. The free plan covers everything this session needs, and no card is requested.
  1. Make it public. Claiming applies the account default visibility, which is private, so the URL shows a login screen to everyone except the owner. Click Make public in the dialog, or from the project overview afterwards.
  1. Open the live URL from the project overview and confirm it loads. Renaming the subdomain to something readable lives under Project configuration.
Close the loop Have everyone drop their live URL into the group chat once it's up. That's the session's finish line, and a quick roll call of who made it all the way through.
